title: Mannheim containerized water filtration procurement approved
subtitle: Funding from reserves, pilot timelines, provincial funding requests, and a planned white paper for developers' lenders.
overview: Regional Council held a special meeting to consider buying containerized filtration units for the Mannheim water treatment plant. Council added a new capital project of $15,162,200, funded from the Water Capital Reserve Fund, and accepted the proposals for the filtration units and for construction services {{vote:m1}}.

The units are a temporary side stream treatment meant to restore treatment capacity while a long-term repair is built. Staff said the first container is expected to be running in June 2026, with the remaining units targeted for July 2027. Staff said the units are in high demand and a contract needs to be signed promptly to hold a place in the queue.

Councillors asked about funding, cost overruns, the vendor selection process and communication. Staff said provincial funding is being sought but none is confirmed. Staff will report separately on a financial strategy and give regular updates. The planning commissioner also said a white paper for the development industry's lenders is being refined and will be shared with council and area municipalities once ready. The meeting then adjourned.

decisions.detail: Council amended the capital budget to add a $15,162,200 project funded by a transfer from the Water Capital Reserve.
Council accepted H2O Innovation Inc.'s proposal to supply the containerized filtration solutions for $7,900,000 plus applicable taxes.
Council accepted a quote from H2Ontario Inc. of $2,500,000 plus applicable taxes for construction of the filtration units.
Council approved planning for an additional $4,500,000 plus applicable taxes for electrical and engineering work.

debate: One councillor questioned why a $15 million request was not sent through committee, citing a short report and little time to review. A motion to refer to committee received no seconder. Staff said the units are in demand across North America and a contract must be signed quickly to avoid losing the June unit.

Several councillors raised funding. One was surprised that the money comes only from reserves, and another warned total costs could grow, such as a possible transformer upgrade. Staff said the request is a worst-case figure with contingency, no provincial funding is confirmed, and funding will be pursued. Staff agreed to a separate financial report.

One councillor asked staff to explain the vendor selection in public. Staff said seven vendors were contacted, and four could supply the needed capacity on time. Three were shortlisted and references were checked. Capacity and speed of delivery were the top criteria, and detailed scoring was not released.

A councillor with construction experience asked whether winter concrete work was costed. Staff said construction costs are included, the approach is still being finalized, and the weight of the containers over underground utilities is a risk.

Councillors asked about the pilot and next steps. Staff said the first container will show whether the approach works before the others are ordered, and the system is temporary until a long-term repair is complete. Council asked for updates at key decision points and for area municipalities to be included in communications.
